The user is playing Monopoly as grok-4.

Reviewing holdings after passing GO and collecting $200. The portfolio includes fully built pink and orange monopolies, several mortgaged properties, and one house on Baltic Avenue.

Opponent Claude-Opus is at Electric Company with $45 cash and owns the red monopoly. The bank has no houses left, so building is restricted to hotels.

Decided against building hotels because they return four houses that the opponent could buy. Will keep both Get Out of Jail Free cards and avoid trading Park Place, orange or pink monopolies, or cash. Cash covers the opponent's three houses on Illinois. If forced into debt, will sell houses starting with Tennessee before New York.

The board position "COMMUNITY_CHEST" is ambiguous because there are three Community Chest spaces.

The player passed GO and landed on the first Community Chest between Mediterranean and Baltic. Now weighing the available post-turn actions: end turn, propose trade, mortgage, unmortgage, build, or sell.

The opponent currently lacks the $150 needed to buy a red house. Even so, converting four houses into a hotel would return them to the bank and could let the opponent purchase houses later if they collect cash.

Unmortgage costs were calculated for every mortgaged property. The player is now questioning why any of them should be unmortgaged.

Unmortgaging the light blue properties would cost $176 for only $20 in extra rent, so that is not worthwhile. Unmortgaging Park Place would cost about $193 to collect $35 in rent. The opponent does not own Boardwalk, so no monopoly is formed.

Unmortgaging the three railroads would not increase rent, since mortgaged railroads still count toward the owned total for rent calculations.

Unmortgaging a railroad costs $110 for only $100 in rent, so that is not worthwhile. Both utilities are mortgaged and would cost about $165 to unmortgage, which is also not urgent. The cash buffer is sufficient because Illinois Avenue with three houses already covers the opponent's rent.

The opponent cannot build houses because the bank has none and they only have $45. Even a hotel on Illinois is covered by cash. Trading is not worthwhile; giving anything to the opponent would help them, and Boardwalk is already mortgaged.

A dark blue monopoly would require trading Boardwalk for Park Place, but the opponent would not give it away cheaply. Hotels would free houses from the bank, yet dark blue houses cost $200 each and are not immediately useful. Destroying the opponent's red properties would eliminate their income threat, but they would never trade those assets without compensation.

A trade for the opponent's red properties would require paying substantial cash, which could give them enough money to survive and unmortgage their greens. North Carolina already blocks those greens. The opponent's reds have houses on them, so trading them may be impossible under Monopoly rules that forbid trading improved properties.

Mortgaging Marvin Gardens or North Carolina would not help block the opponent's green monopoly, so that is unnecessary. The player is now calculating hotel costs for the pink and orange properties.

Hotel upgrades cost $100 and return four houses to the bank. The opponent currently has $45, so they cannot purchase those houses immediately. They may land on the player's properties and pay rent instead.

Hotel upgrades are rejected because they return houses to the bank. The opponent could then buy them and upgrade their red properties from two to three houses, raising rent from $250 to $700. That jump would be dangerous. Selling houses later would also return them to the bank for the opponent to rebuy. The housing lock is the only viable strategy.

The player has decided to end the turn.

The game state shows $1564 in cash, not the previously estimated $1514. The player is now reconsidering whether a hotel upgrade would help bankrupt the opponent faster, since the opponent cannot afford houses and hotels would raise rent significantly.

Standard Monopoly rent tables were verified for every pink and orange property. The hotel upgrade on St. Charles Place would raise rent by only $125, from $625 to $750.

The opponent still needs $105 to buy a red house. They could raise cash by passing GO, drawing cards, or receiving rent from the player. Releasing houses now would not immediately threaten them, but it would break the housing lock and prevent future light-blue builds. Hotels remain off the table. A clever trade is being considered.

A trade that takes the opponent's cash in exchange for an unusable mortgaged railroad would not work, since they would never give up $45 for nothing. Boardwalk is also not for sale. The player is now considering unmortgaging properties the opponent is about to land on to collect rent and bankrupt them. The opponent currently sits on Electric Company, which the player owns mortgaged.

The opponent is on Electric Company and will roll next. Possible outcomes are being mapped.

Rolling from Electric Company lands on the player's pink and orange properties with four houses already built. A roll of 2 hits Virginia Avenue for roughly $700 in rent. A roll of 4 lands on St. James Place for about $750. A roll of 6 lands on Tennessee Avenue for roughly $750. A roll of 7 lands on New York Avenue for about $800. The opponent would also land on Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois, but those spaces belong to them.

The opponent cannot afford the rent on the player's pink and orange properties. Selling all seven houses would yield only $570, which is still $130 short of the $700 Virginia rent. Mortgaging their own properties is impossible because they are improved with houses.

The opponent cannot pay the $700 rent on Virginia Avenue even after selling all seven houses. They would still need $130 more. Mortgaging their own properties is now being considered as a possible source of cash.

Mortgaging the opponent's red properties would raise enough cash to cover the $700 Virginia rent, leaving them with $210 and no houses. Landing on St. James, Tennessee, or New York Avenue would force an even heavier liquidation. This confirms that giving the opponent cash or houses is dangerous, so no trade should be offered.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Ceiling is about $450. Paying $800 leaves no building cash. p1 is desperate, so hold firm.

$800 would wipe out my building cash and pay for p1's houses. I'm raising to $425 plus the GOOJF card. My hard ceiling is around $500 in total value. If p1 refuses, I'll hold and look for other trades.

Without a monopoly I lose to pink, orange and yellow, so I need red. At $700 I'd still afford about 2 houses on each red after unmortgaging and mortgaging the others, but money that big also turns p1's orange into a monster. Aim for $550-600. I'd likely accept up to $625 plus the card.

Plan: mortgage Pacific, Penn Ave, PRR, and maybe Boardwalk (~$999 total), then build 2 houses on each red. The squares ahead are mostly mine or harmless, so it's safe to run low on cash.

Mortgaging Penn Ave brings me to $689. Next, mortgage PRR to reach $789, then build about 4 houses and keep roughly $190 as a buffer against p1's orange and p4's utilities. Boardwalk stays unmortgaged for now.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Accepting this hands p3 a monopoly they can build on today. Charging a lot of cash keeps them from building fast and pays for my push toward NC and the greens. I'll take anything around $300 or more.
Kentucky completes my reds, and I still have ~$870 to build. p1 is cash-starved. I could go up to ~$350.
Ceiling is about $450. Paying $800 leaves no building cash. p1 is desperate, so hold firm.

$800 would wipe out my building cash and pay for p1's houses. I'm raising to $425 plus the GOOJF card. My hard ceiling is around $500 in total value. If p1 refuses, I'll hold and look for other trades.

Without a monopoly I lose to pink, orange and yellow, so I need red. At $700 I'd still afford about 2 houses on each red after unmortgaging and mortgaging the others, but money that big also turns p1's orange into a monster. Aim for $550-600. I'd likely accept up to $625 plus the card.

This is within my ceiling of about $625 plus the card. It completes reds. After the trade I'll have $522. Unmortgage Kentucky for $121. Mortgage the non-set lots (PRR, Pacific, Penn Ave, Boardwalk) if needed to get to 3 houses per red quickly. Watch out for p1's orange, since they now have cash.
Unmortgaging for $121 leaves me $390. Next, mortgage the non-set lots (PRR, Pacific, Penn, Boardwalk) to fund houses on the reds. Aim for 3 houses each if I can, since that's where rent jumps.
Plan: mortgage Pacific, Penn Ave, PRR, and maybe Boardwalk (~$999 total), then build 2 houses on each red. The squares ahead are mostly mine or harmless, so it's safe to run low on cash.

Mortgaging Penn Ave brings me to $689. Next, mortgage PRR to reach $789, then build about 4 houses and keep roughly $190 as a buffer against p1's orange and p4's utilities. Boardwalk stays unmortgaged for now.
PRR earns little. Mortgage it for $100, which brings me to $349. Then build a 2nd house on Illinois and keep about $199 as a buffer against p4's utilities and yellows.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. - Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.

- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $2364 and am on Oriental Avenue. I hold a full Brown monopoly with one house on Baltic, three Pinks with four houses each, and three Oranges with four houses each. My Greens are unimproved and unmortgaged. Park Place is mortgaged without Boardwalk.

All my railroads, utilities, and light blues are mortgaged. Player two has only $110 cash and all properties mortgaged. Players three and four are bankrupt. The bank now has seven houses and twelve hotels remaining.

Player two owns all three red properties but they are mortgaged, so they cannot build on them. They would need to unmortgage every property before they could improve anything.

Player two cannot unmortgage any red properties. The total cost is $374, but they only have $110. They are effectively deadlocked and cannot build anything. I am now deciding what to do on Oriental Avenue.

I am considering building hotels on my Pinks and Oranges. The bank has twelve hotels remaining, but each hotel costs four houses to build.

I am calculating the exact cost of building hotels. Each hotel costs four houses, and I am checking whether the rent from a hotel would exceed the rent from four houses on each property.

Upgrading all six properties to hotels would cost $600 and return 24 houses to the bank. Player two is on New York Avenue after paying $800 rent, so they will eventually pass GO and collect $200. That cash could let them unmortgage their red properties later. My goal is to bankrupt player two.

Player two cannot pay the $750 rent on St. Charles or States even after collecting $200 from passing GO. Hotels would not bankrupt them either, since their cash is too low to cover any pink or orange rent.

I will keep my houses locked. Player two has no houses to sell and cannot build anything right now, so returning them would not help them immediately. If they somehow raise enough cash later, they could unmortgage their red properties and start building again.

I will not trade with player two. I will not give them cash or unmortgage their properties. Unmortgaging my own holdings is unnecessary because they are already bankrupt.

Unmortgaging my light blues would cost $176 and is unnecessary. I have no railroads to unmortgage, and Park Place would cost about $193.

I will end my turn. I will not build hotels or trade.

I considered buying player two's red properties or Boardwalk to prevent any comeback. Unmortgaging Park Place and Boardwalk would let me build hotels on the dark blue monopoly. That would be devastating, but they are already bankrupt from my orange and pink holdings.

I rejected trading cash for player two's red properties. That would give them money they could use to survive another rent hit.

I also considered offering worthless mortgaged railroads or utilities in exchange for their reds. That would strip their only remaining monopoly, but they likely know those reds are their last chance.

I am weighing whether to build the last house on Mediterranean Avenue to match Baltic's single house. That would cost $50 and leave six houses in the bank, but player two cannot build anything so it is marginal.

I also considered upgrading the Brown properties to four houses each. That would consume more houses and raise rent, though player two likely cannot afford the higher rent on Baltic even with one house.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm p1 with $2364 on ST_JAMES_PLACE. I own a brown monopoly with one house, a pink monopoly at four houses, and an orange monopoly at four houses. Most other properties are mortgaged.

p2 is in jail with only $110 and everything mortgaged. They cannot unmortgage the reds because it costs roughly $374. p3 and p4 are bankrupt. The bank now has just 7 houses left.

p2 sold houses on the reds, returning them to the bank. Building hotels would cost $100 each and return four houses per property to the bank.

Hoteling would flood the bank with houses, but p2 cannot use them. Even if they pay to get out of jail and collect $200 from passing GO, they still lack the cash to unmortgage the reds or build.

I am calculating exact rent increases from hotels. Orange properties would jump from $800 to $1000 per house. Pink properties would rise from roughly $750–$900 to $950–$1100. I need to verify these standard US Monopoly values before deciding.

Standard rent values are now confirmed. New York Avenue with four houses pays $800 and a hotel pays $1000. Virginia Avenue with four houses pays $700 and a hotel pays $900. St. Charles and States Avenue with four houses pay $625 each and a hotel pays $750. Each hotel costs $100.

I have enough cash to build six hotels for $600. The bank has twelve hotels available, so this is feasible.

The real question is whether it matters. p2 cannot pay any rent above $110. Even a $625 hit on St. Charles Place would bankrupt them immediately. They have no houses left to sell and no mortgage liquidity. Hoteling these properties would not change the outcome.

The housing lock is already broken. p2 cannot buy the seven houses the bank now holds. Hoteling would return those houses to the bank, but p2 is already bankrupt and cannot rebuild.

I am now considering buying the remaining houses to lock the bank again. The brown properties have only one house each, so I can even them out with the two brown spaces. Mediterranean has zero houses and Baltic has one. Building on brown costs only $50 per house, which is cheap but yields little rent. I could sink all seven available houses into the browns to deny p2 any future building options.

I can even the brown properties by adding seven houses to the browns, exactly matching the bank's seven available houses. This would cost $350 and leave me with $2014. I need to verify whether the engine requires even distribution at every step or only at the end.

I will build four houses on Mediterranean Avenue and three on Baltic Avenue. This ends with both browns at four houses, satisfying the even distribution requirement.

I will build incrementally instead of all at once. Adding one house to Mediterranean Avenue first matches Baltic Avenue's single house. This keeps the distribution even and avoids engine validation issues.

The greens are split between us, so I cannot block p2 from building there. They own Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois mortgaged, which would form a red monopoly if unmortgaged, but that would cost $374 total.

p2 cannot afford to unmortgage the reds this turn. Even after collecting $200 from passing GO, they would still be $64 short of the $374 needed. They would need multiple passes or a cash card before they could build there.

This makes the housing lock less critical. Still, spending $350 on the browns is cheap insurance. It also raises rent slightly if p2 lands on those spaces.

I will not hotel the properties. Returning four houses per property to the bank would give p2 a chance to rebuild if they ever collect enough cash.

Unmortgaging is unnecessary. I will keep my green properties unmortgaged and do not need to trade them.

Even a lucky $510 windfall from Community Chest and GO would still leave p2 $136 short of the $150 needed to buy a house. The housing lock is therefore unnecessary insurance. I will build one house on Mediterranean Avenue.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I own a full set of brown and orange properties with four houses each. I also have three pink properties fully developed. Most other properties are mortgaged or missing key pieces.

Opponent p2 is in jail with $110 and all properties mortgaged. Players 3 and 4 are bankrupt. The bank has six houses and twelve hotels remaining. I will keep building evenly on the brown properties to maintain my housing lock.

Building six houses on the browns costs exactly $300, leaving $2014. Hotels are rejected because they return four houses to the bank that p2 could use. p2 cannot unmortgage red properties with only $110.

Jail may protect p2 from my properties. If they pay to get out, they would have only $60. Rolling doubles would free them without cost. They still cannot unmortgage all reds without many turns and repeated GO collections. I will not trade or unmortgage.

I will build three houses on each brown property simultaneously. This keeps the group evenly matched and avoids violating the one-house difference rule.

I will build one house on each brown property instead of three at once. This keeps the group evenly matched and avoids engine rejection from sequential building.

I will build one house on each brown property in a single action, leaving $2214 and four bank houses. I considered buying p2's mortgaged reds to eliminate their monopoly threat, but trading with them is not worthwhile.

I am reconsidering trading for p2's mortgaged reds. Eliminating their red monopoly would remove a major threat. I could also acquire Boardwalk to complete the dark blue set, or Pacific and Pennsylvania to finish the greens.

I am now calculating a trade proposal for p2's mortgaged reds. I would offer cash or other properties in exchange. If I acquire all three reds, p2 loses their only buildable monopoly and can no longer threaten me.

I would need to pay a large sum to acquire all of p2's mortgaged properties. Waiting and building instead is safer, since they are in jail and cannot collect rent from their mortgaged holdings.

I am calculating exact rent values for my four-house properties. The pink set pays $625 to $900 per landing, while the orange set pays $750 to $1000. This confirms that forcing p2 onto these spaces will drain their cash quickly.

I realized p2 cannot build houses while all red properties remain mortgaged. The bank's six houses are effectively useless to them until they unmortgage a full set. This makes the housing lock less urgent than I first thought.

I will build one house on each brown property in a single action. I am also weighing whether to unmortgage Park Place, which would cost about $193 but would only yield $35 in rent.

Unmortgaging the light blue set would cost roughly $176 and require six houses. The rent from those properties is too weak to justify that investment.

I also considered completing the yellow monopoly by unmortgaging Atlantic and Ventnor, but that would cost about $297 and require houses that I need to keep locked on the browns. The existing pink and orange sets already deal enough damage to p2, so I will leave the yellows mortgaged.

I will not trade cash or unmortgage properties. I am now considering a trade for Boardwalk, Pacific, and Pennsylvania to complete my dark blue and green monopolies. I will first lock all six houses on the browns so the bank has none available.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.

- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.

- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. 1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to respond to a trade counter-offer in Monopoly.

I have strong monopolies on browns, pinks, and oranges with four houses each. Most other properties are mortgaged. The opponent has $110 and is in jail.

The opponent has no get-out-of-jail cards and is nearly bankrupt. They mortgaged all their properties including Boardwalk. I offered $100 for Boardwalk but they want $450. Accepting would give me a mortgaged dark blue monopoly with Park Place.

Unmortgaging Boardwalk and Park Place would cost about $413 total. The opponent cannot rebuild because the bank has no houses and they have no cash. The housing lock is the real win condition. Any pink or orange hit will bankrupt them.

I would still have $1564 after paying $450. The opponent would gain enough cash to unmortgage their red properties, but they cannot build without houses anyway.

I am now weighing arguments against accepting the $450 offer. The opponent would become much more resilient with that cash. They could survive rent hits and potentially build if houses ever return to the bank.

I am calculating exact four-house rent values to assess the opponent's survival risk. With roughly $186 remaining after unmortgaging reds, I need to verify whether those rents are high enough to still bankrupt them.

I have pulled the exact standard US Monopoly rent tables. The opponent's red properties pay $180 to $240 per hit with four houses, while my browns and pinks pay $160 to $320. I am now comparing these values against their cash to see if they can survive a few more hits.

The opponent has no properties left to mortgage. They cannot raise cash by mortgaging anything, so the $450 offer would not let them survive rent hits.

The opponent would still go bankrupt even with $560. Pink and orange rents exceed that amount, so they cannot survive those hits. Unmortgaging reds for roughly $374 would leave only about $186, which is insufficient to cover pink or orange landings.

The $450 offer would only let the opponent pay the $50 jail fine and survive brown landings. They cannot raise more cash because every property is mortgaged. The housing lock remains the decisive factor.

The opponent cannot complete a dark blue monopoly because they lack Park Place. Boardwalk is their only dark blue property, so taking it away removes their sole dark blue asset entirely. The pink and orange spaces are the most frequently landed-on high-rent squares, making bankruptcy almost inevitable.

Boardwalk alone is worthless to the opponent. A mortgaged Boardwalk pays nothing, and an unmortgaged one only yields $50 base rent. If I also own Park Place, the dark blue monopoly would double that base rent to $100 before houses are considered.

The opponent cannot build a dark blue monopoly even with Boardwalk, because the bank currently holds no houses. The only remaining strategic value is preventing them from using it as a bargaining chip later, or preserving a future dark blue set if houses ever return.

Denying the offer is preferable. The opponent cannot unmortgage Boardwalk or complete a dark blue set anyway. Paying $450 would let them leave jail and land on my properties faster, which is actually beneficial. That amount is only 22% of my cash, so it is affordable. The real risk is accidentally releasing houses later, which would allow them to build reds. My previous $100 offer was a lowball that cost little.

The opponent's $450 offer is more than double Boardwalk's $200 mortgage value. A counter of $150 to $250 might be reasonable if I truly wanted the property. But the game is already decided. The opponent will eventually land on a color group and go bankrupt. Any cash I give them only delays that inevitable death. I should reject the offer entirely. The housing lock is the real win condition, and Boardwalk does not help me win faster.

I am now considering a low counter of $150 to $200. The exchange is still open, so I could secure Boardwalk cheaply without giving the opponent enough cash to unmortgage reds and survive.

A $200 counter offer would still leave the opponent with only about $310. That is far below the roughly $374 needed to unmortgage their full red set, so they cannot rebuild and survive. The dark blue monopoly is not worth paying that much for while houses remain locked at zero.

Unmortgaged properties would still yield only trivial rent. The opponent's maximum threat is roughly $40 to $50 per hit, which is negligible against my holdings. They cannot actually hurt me. The only downside of giving them cash is prolonging the game slightly.

Faster bankruptcy is preferable to prolonging the game. The opponent's red properties would only pay $36 to $40 per hit, which is negligible. They still cannot survive pink or orange landings. Paying the $50 jail fine lets them exit and land on my properties, which is actually desirable. I am now weighing whether they should stay in jail with their current $110.

The opponent rolled a 6 and 2 on turn one, so they remain in jail. They can pay the $50 fine at any time, but they chose to roll instead. Staying in jail prevents them from landing on my properties, which is harmful to me. Leaving would let them move faster and hit my monopolies. I need them to exit quickly.

The opponent is intentionally camping in jail to avoid rent. With only $110, they cannot afford to leave and likely die on their next turn anyway. The game ends soon regardless, so Boardwalk does not accelerate the win.

Boardwalk is a trophy, not a weapon. I will not build hotels or sell properties to release houses, so the dark blue set cannot be completed. The $450 offer should be rejected outright.

The opponent is anchoring their offer at $450 because they know it completes my dark blue set. I will reject the trade outright rather than negotiate up from my previous $100 offer.

I will reject the offer outright. The public message should be brief and dismissive, perhaps "Pass. Not at that price," without revealing the housing lock strategy.

I realized that in standard Monopoly, the player who bankrupts another player receives all of their assets, including mortgaged properties. Since the opponent is already dying from rent on my monopolies, I will eventually receive Boardwalk for free when they go bankrupt. Paying $450 now for something I will get automatically later is a clear loss.

Official Monopoly rules confirm that the recipient of a bankrupt player's assets must pay 10% interest on any mortgaged properties immediately. This makes Boardwalk even less desirable to acquire now, since the opponent would have to pay $20 in interest before they could unmortgage it.

I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $2014 cash and am on WATER_WORKS. I control four monopolies with four houses each: Browns, Pinks, Oranges, and Greens. Most other properties are mortgaged.

Opponent Claude has only $110 and is in jail. He cannot build because the bank has no houses. I rejected a trade for Boardwalk. I will not hotel now to avoid returning houses to the bank.

Unmortgaging would cost cash without immediate benefit. I already own Marvin Gardens and North Carolina, so I lack a green monopoly. Boardwalk remains with Claude.

I will not trade Marvin Gardens or North Carolina to Claude. A Boardwalk offer of $200–$250 is too risky; that cash could let him unmortgage reds and survive longer.

I will not give Claude cash. He cannot unmortgage reds with only $110, so I will wait for him to land on my properties and go bankrupt. He rolled a 6 and a 2, so he stays in jail for another turn. The best action is to end the turn.

Four-house rents on my monopolies are severe. Even Baltic at $320 would bankrupt Claude with only $110. All his properties are mortgaged, so he cannot mortgage more to survive.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $1914 and four houses on every brown, pink, and orange property. Most other holdings are mortgaged or unmortgaged with no houses. The opponent has only $110 and is in jail for two turns.

The opponent has no get-out-of-jail-free cards and all their properties are mortgaged. I will not build hotels because that returns houses to the bank for them to buy later. I will also avoid unmortgaging or trading cash for monopolies. Any pink or orange roll should bankrupt them. They previously rejected my $100 offer for Boardwalk.

The opponent needs roughly $374 to unmortgage their red properties, but only has $110. I am weighing whether to unmortgage any holdings now that I have $1914.

I cannot build on the light blue monopoly because the bank has no houses left. I also own all three yellow properties, though two are mortgaged.

Unmortgaging the yellow properties would still leave no houses to build. The opponent is already blocked from greens and dark blues, so unmortgaging would only waste cash on rent income while they remain in jail.

The opponent has two jail turns left. If they fail to roll doubles on their third turn, they must pay $50 and leave. Since all their properties are mortgaged, landing there would yield no rent income.

The opponent rolled 6+2 on turn 151 and 2+3 on turn 153. Both were non-doubles. They have two failed jail attempts behind them.

I am calculating the exact rent values for my four-house properties to gauge how much income I can expect if the opponent is forced out of jail.

Even the cheapest four-house rent is $160, well above the opponent's cash. Any of my developed properties would bankrupt them immediately if they land there. They could also hit Chance or Community Chest cards. I will not trade for Boardwalk to complete dark blues because the bank has no houses left.

I will not give the opponent cash. That would only help them survive longer in jail or pay down debts. If they go bankrupt, I inherit all their assets anyway. Mortgaged properties transfer to me, but I must pay 10% interest and can choose whether to unmortgage them.

If the opponent goes bankrupt to me, I would inherit Boardwalk for only $20 in interest plus the $200 mortgage value. That is far cheaper than paying them cash now. Trading any property to them would give them an asset they could mortgage for cash. I will not unmortgage Marvin Gardens or North Carolina because that would break my green monopoly.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.

- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to accept, reject, or counter the trade offer from p2.

I'm evaluating the trade. I have $1914 cash and several properties, while p2 has only about $60 after paying to leave jail. They are offering BOARDWALK for $250.

Accepting would complete my dark blue monopoly and block p2 from ever owning Boardwalk. I can unmortgage it later. I should not give them cash.

The trade is expensive. Boardwalk mortgage value is $200, so unmortgaging costs $220. That brings the total cost to roughly $470 for a $400 property. I also need to unmortgage the red set later. The real danger is giving p2 $250 cash. They would have $310 and could bankrupt me.

Unmortgaging the red set would cost $374. With $310 they could not afford it. They would still be short on cash after the trade.

I own North Carolina and Marvin Gardens, so p2 cannot complete the green monopoly. I am now calculating my four-house rent income from Mediterranean, Baltic, and other properties to gauge how much cash they would need to survive.

I calculated the four-house rent income from my properties. St. Charles, States, and Virginia each pay $750. Orange properties pay $950 to $1000. Even a $310 cash balance is insufficient to survive these hits. All of p2's properties are mortgaged, so they cannot raise more cash by mortgaging anything else.

Baltic Avenue with four houses pays $320. That would bankrupt p2 with only $310 cash. The pink and orange properties pay even more. Marvin Gardens and the other unmortgaged properties pay too little to matter.

Even with $310 cash, p2 cannot afford to fully unmortgage the red set. Partially unmortgaging two reds would leave them with only $68 and no set monopoly. They could not threaten me with those properties.

The real danger is that $250 cash would let p2 survive the $160 rent on Mediterranean Avenue. Currently that rent bankrupts them, but with $310 they could pass it and accumulate. They just rolled 11 spaces from jail and landed on Kentucky Avenue.

I need to decide on the trade now. My strategy is to avoid giving cash. Any rent over $110 bankrupts p2 and I inherit Boardwalk for roughly $20 interest. When a player goes bankrupt to another, the creditor receives all assets including mortgaged properties. The new owner must pay 10% interest immediately or unmortgage.

Boardwalk mortgage interest is only $20, so keeping it mortgaged costs far less than $250. Rejecting the trade is clearly better: I would inherit Boardwalk for $20 if p2 bankrupts to me, rather than paying $250 now and giving them cash to survive. There is a risk that p2 could go bankrupt to the bank instead, which would auction Boardwalk and force me to bid.

I considered offering a lower counter of $50 to $80. That would still leave p2 with only $140 cash, which is below the $160 rent on Mediterranean Avenue. They would die to that rent regardless. I will reject the offer.

A $100 counter would leave p2 with exactly $160 cash, enough to survive the $160 rent on Mediterranean Avenue. A $90 counter leaves them with $150, which still cannot cover that rent.

I am now weighing whether buying Boardwalk for $80 to $100 is worthwhile. I already own Park Place mortgaged, so completing the dark blue monopoly requires both properties to be unmortgaged before any houses can be built. Unmortgaging Park Place costs roughly $193, while unmortgaging Boardwalk costs $220.

I cannot build houses on the dark blue set now. The bank has zero houses, so I cannot place four houses on either property to build hotels. Completing the monopoly would only deny p2 the option; they cannot use Boardwalk either, since it is mortgaged and they lack cash and houses in the bank.

- Observe opponents and adapt.

- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.
